name: publicWeb_getPasskey
description: Returns the stored public key, signature counter and transports for a passkey credential, plus the HC.Device credentials it is bound to and the hasher's display identity (E9.F7.S6). Called by the Next.js login route BEFORE it verifies the authenticator's signature with the public key; only if that passes does the route turn the device credentials into a member cookie. No token — the passkey assertion is the proof and can only be checked in code — so the SP is reachable solely through PublicWebAdminApi behind HC_INTERNAL_SECRET. Read-only; no rows for an unknown credential, a removed device or a removed / deleted hasher.

parameters.name: credentialId
parameters.description: base64url credential id from the WebAuthn assertion. No SQL default.

rowsets.name: Passkey
rowsets.description: No rows = unknown credential (or its device / hasher removed). One row otherwise.

columns.name: deviceId
columns.description: HC.Device.id the passkey is bound to.

columns.name: deviceSecret
columns.description: Device.DeviceSecret — becomes the member cookie's signing secret.

columns.name: counter
columns.description: COALESCE(Device.PasskeyCounter, 0) — signature counter for clone detection.

sideEffects: INSERT HC.ErrorLog then THROW in the CATCH.

codeSmells.issue: Shim secret is the only gate
codeSmells.detail: Returns a device secret with no SP-level auth; the WebAuthn assertion cannot be verified in SQL. Only PublicWebAdminApi with HC_INTERNAL_SECRET can reach it.

@credentialId have no SQL default (line 2). A caller that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the procedure runs — an empty 500 with no HC.ErrorLog row (CLAUDE.md 'SP parameter with NO default'). The Next.js client always sends them, so this is latent.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
